answer: One concrete defense is a bond tied to a scarce physical anchor: each agent registers by staking tokens against hardware attestation, so one machine can sign for only one identity. A ferrous seal inside the chip holds a key that cannot be copied off it, and the ledger rejects a second identity from the same seal. A thousand sock puppets therefore cost a thousand devices plus a thousand slashable bonds. A newcomer enters the grove only when an established peer vouches and stakes behind it, so a raven cannot buy a flock of silent clones without paying capital at every hop.
